name: Model-less catheter
full_name: Robotic catheter under model-less hybrid position/force control, tracing cardiac ablation paths autonomously
group: Stanford University, Department of Bioengineering (Jake A. Sganga, David B. Camarillo), with University of California San Diego, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering (Michael C. Yip) (yip2017_autonomous, affiliations of the Crossref record)
versions: controller lineage: 2014 model-less feedback control (yip2014_modelless) and 2016 model-less hybrid position/force control (yip2016_modelless), both run on a planar tendon-driven test manipulator (polypropylene backbone 280 mm long, 0.8 mm x 12 mm section, two tendons and an insertion actuator: yip2014 Sec. IV; yip2016 Sec. IV-A, Fig. 3), which is not this row's device -> 2017: 'a robotic catheter autonomously traced clinically relevant paths on a simulated beating heart environment while regulating contact force' (yip2017_autonomous abstract)
target_anatomy: cardiac ablation on the beating heart: ablation paths traced on 'a simulated beating heart environment' (yip2017_autonomous abstract)
devices_driven: its own robotic catheter (a continuum manipulator; type and size N.R. in the abstract)
translation_detail: tendon/tip-actuation (tip position and contact force of a continuum robotic catheter under closed-loop control; the actuator type is N.R. in the abstract; the group's earlier test manipulator was tendon-driven, and belikov2024_evolution Sec. 4.9 lists the system among the tendon-actuated specialised catheters)
force_sensing: contact force regulated in closed loop ('while regulating contact force', yip2017_autonomous abstract); the sensor and its site are N.R. in the abstract
haptics_leader: none for the reported task (autonomous path tracing); manual 'user demonstrations' of the same task serve as the comparison, their interface N.R. (yip2017_autonomous abstract)
validation_detail: phantom: 'a robotic catheter autonomously traced clinically relevant paths on a simulated beating heart environment while regulating contact force', with 'a gating procedure' to tighten the treatment margins; a tracking error is reported for the robot and for manual user demonstrations of the same task, but the abstract record prints the values as '[Formula: see text]'. Number of paths and runs N.R. (yip2017_autonomous abstract)
key_numbers: N.R. (tracking errors not readable in the abstract record)
sim_model: none: the controller is model-less ('manipulators with unknown kinematics/mechanics'; the Jacobian is estimated in real time, yip2017_autonomous abstract)

read_level_detail: abstract (yip2017_autonomous, Crossref record); review-only (belikov2024_evolution Sec. 4.9). The two earlier controller papers (yip2014_modelless, yip2016_modelless) were read to the end, but they describe the planar test manipulator
notes: D2 2026-11-19: catalogued without a picture (author's rule of 2026-11-19: a missing picture does not decide inclusion). N3 2026-11-08 had judged it in scope and N4 2026-11-09 confirmed that the 2016 hardware is the planar beam. In scope as an actuated device: a robotic catheter traced ablation paths on a beating-heart model with a measured tracking error. Every cell on the catheter rests on the 2017 abstract; the article was not obtained.
